Jordan — thanks for the MAP and the clear checkpoints. We can absolutely map pricing to each milestone. Draft below is a starting point; Ben and Marissa I've looped you for commercial approval.

Proposal (draft):
- Pilot (month 0–1): trial rate of $0.004/token with a $10k credit applied to month 1 bill for integration work (one-time).
- Early ramp (months 2–3): committed minimum throughput (QPS) of 150 rps; discounted rate $0.0035/token once committed QPS is met for the month.
- Committed run (months 4–6+): if customer commits to a 12-month reserved capacity at closing, step down to $0.0028/token and access to Dedicated burst capacity.

Checkpoint gating:
- Pilot accepted: sign-off on MAP + acceptance test pass (see MAP section 2.1).
- Early ramp unlocked: telemetry shows 7 consecutive days meeting 70% of committed QPS and completion of integration tasks in SOW.
- Committed run: countersigned contract with reserved commitment and agreed SLAs.

Open items:
- Exact ramp-credit mechanics (is the $10k applied as credit or monthly rebate?).
- Whether Acme wants a usage cap in month 1 (we can cap to avoid surprise).
- DocuSign path for the conditional SOW / signature flow.

If this aligns roughly, Ben can confirm discount bands and Marissa can approve any exception on the ramp credit. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Looping in my notes after reviewing Logan's draft. I attached a redlines spreadsheet with revised discount thresholds (pricing-redlines.xlsx). TL;DR: we can shore up the numbers but would like the following guardrails to avoid margin bleed: 

- Make pilot credit a contra invoice credit (one-time) rather than a monthly rebate — cleaner for Revenue recognition.
- Early ramp discount should auto-revert if 3 consecutive months fall below 60% of committed QPS. That protects us during failed ramps.
- For committed run, require a 30-day notice for any downscale of reserved capacity; concessions only on a case-by-case basis.

Also flagging approval needed from Marissa on a $10k upfront credit as an exception to standard policy (we usually run smaller credits tied to technical milestones). If Acme is large and strategic, I'm fine approving but want a Exec approval path documented.

Attachments: pricing-redlines.xlsx

—Ben
